title: Euclid's Data (Δεδομένα · Dedomena)
edition_greek: Euclidis Data cum commentario Marini et scholiis antiquis, ed. Heinrich Menge (Euclidis Opera Omnia, Vol. VI, Leipzig: B. G. Teubner, 1896)
edition_english: Literal GEOMETOR translation from Menge's 1896 non-Theonine Greek text (Vat. gr. 190), collated with Robert Simson's critical English edition (1762 / 1806) and Thomas L. Heath (1921 / 1926)

units.title: Unit 0: Marinus's Protheoria & Definitions 1–15
units.subtitle: Epistemology of Givenness (Δεδομένον) and the Fifteen Foundational Definitions
units.summary: Marinus of Neapolis's philosophical introduction classifying τεταγμένον (ordered), γνώριμον (known), πόριμον (procurable), and ῥητόν (rational), followed by Euclid's 12 authentic definitions of magnitude, ratio, species, position, circles, and affine-ratio excess/defect, plus the 3 bracketed post-Euclidean scholia (Defs. 13–15).

units.title: Unit 1: Magnitudes & Ratios (Propositions 1–24)
units.subtitle: Pure Algebraic Closure of Given Magnitudes, Ratios, and Affine-Ratio Equations
units.summary: Deductive closure of given magnitudes and ratios over Elements Book V: addition, subtraction, inversion, composition, division, ex aequali chains, affine-linear offset relations (δοθέντι μεῖζον ἢ ἐν λόγῳ), non-singular linear combinations (D.22–D.23), and geometric mean proportions (D.24).

units.title: Unit 2: Position, Angles & Parallel Loci (Propositions 25–38)
units.subtitle: Straight Lines Given in Position, Angular Rays, and Parallel Locus Determination
units.summary: Transition from abstract magnitudes to planar geometry: uniqueness of line-line intersections (D.25), endpoints and directions of segments (D.26–D.30), neusis/circle distance meets (D.31), inclined transversals across parallels (D.32–D.33), and parallel ratio-division loci through a fixed pole (D.34–D.38).

units.title: Unit 3: Triangles & Polygons Given in Species (Propositions 39–55)
units.subtitle: Similarity Invariants, Triangle Rigidity Criteria, and Area-to-Side Scaling
units.summary: Constructive determination of triangles up to similarity (εἴδει) from SSS-ratios (D.39), AAA (D.40), SAS-ratio (D.41), side-ratios (D.42), right-SSA (D.43), general SSA bifurcation with obtuse/acute diorismos (D.44), sum/difference of sides (D.45–D.46), decomposing rectilinear polygons into triangles (D.47), and quadratic area-scaling of figures given in species (D.48–D.55).

units.title: Unit 4: Application of Areas, Quadratics & Cosine Projections (Propositions 56–67)
units.subtitle: Geometric Algebra of Parabolic, Elliptic & Hyperbolic Areas and Oblique Triangle Projections
units.summary: Equiangular parallelograms and parabolic division of areas (D.56–D.57), quadratic root extraction via elliptic and hyperbolic application of areas (D.58–D.59) and gnomons (D.60), altitude-to-base ratios (D.61–D.63), generalized Law of Cosines projections in obtuse and acute triangles (D.64–D.65), area-product law BD·BC : △ABC (D.66), and the algebraic identity (a+b)² − c² (D.67).

units.title: Unit 5: Proportional Parallelograms, Triangles & Four-Line Relations (Propositions 68–83)
units.subtitle: Compound Side-Ratios, Reciprocal Proportions, Simson's Lemma, and Four-Line Cross-Multiplications
units.summary: Compound ratio calculus for equiangular and supplementary-angle parallelograms and triangles (D.68–D.75), dropped-altitude ratios in species-given triangles (D.76), duplicated/corollarial area-species bridges (D.77–D.78), inscribed circle-triangle similarity lemmas and area-product determination (D.79–D.80), and four-line proportional transformations (D.81–D.83).

units.title: Unit 6: Hyperbolic/Elliptic Systems, Circles, Chords & Angle Bisectors (Propositions 84–94)
units.subtitle: Canonical Two-Segment Quadratic Systems, Circular Loci, Chord Power, and the Prop. 93 Bisector Theorem
units.summary: Canonical two-line systems xy = A² with x − y = d (D.84), x + y = s (D.85), and x² − y² = C² (D.86); circles given in magnitude and position, inscribed angle loci, and chord/arc determination (D.87–D.89); secant/chord power of a point (D.90–D.92); the celebrated Prop. 93 interior angle-bisector theorem; and its orthogonal chord-reflection corollary (D.94).

definitions.greek_text: Δεδομένα τῷ μεγέθει λέγεται χωρία τε καὶ γραμμαὶ καὶ γωνίαι, οἷς δυνάμεθα ἴσα πορίσασθαι.
definitions.english_text: Spaces, lines, and angles are called given in magnitude to which we can procure equals.
definitions.functional_form: GivenMagnitude(X) := exists constructible X' with X' = X

definitions.greek_text: Λόγος δεδόσθαι λέγεται, ᾧ δυνάμεθα τὸν αὐτὸν πορίσασθαι.
definitions.english_text: A ratio is said to be given to which we can procure an identical ratio.
definitions.functional_form: GivenRatio(A : B) := exists GivenMagnitude(C, D) with A : B = C : D

definitions.greek_text: Εὐθύγραμμα σχήματα τῷ εἴδει δεδόσθαι λέγεται, ὧν αἵ τε γωνίαι δεδομέναι εἰσὶ κατὰ μίαν καὶ οἱ λόγοι τῶν πλευρῶν πρὸς ἀλλήλας δεδομένοι.
definitions.english_text: Rectilineal figures are said to be given in species whose angles are severally given and the ratios of whose sides to one another are given.
definitions.functional_form: GivenSpecies(P) := forall i,j: GivenAngle(ang_i(P)) and GivenRatio(s_i(P) : s_j(P))

definitions.greek_text: Τῇ θέσει δεδόσθαι λέγονται σημεῖά τε καὶ γραμμαὶ καὶ γωνίαι, ἃ τὸν αὐτὸν ἀεὶ τόπον ἐπέχει.
definitions.english_text: Points, lines, and angles are said to be given in position which always occupy the same place.
definitions.functional_form: GivenPosition(X) := X is invariant in the fixed planar reference frame (and constructible)

definitions.greek_text: Κύκλος τῷ μεγέθει δεδόσθαι λέγεται, οὗ δέδοται ἡ ἐκ τοῦ κέντρου τῷ μεγέθει.
definitions.english_text: A circle is said to be given in magnitude whose radius (straight line from the centre) is given in magnitude.

definitions.greek_text: Τῇ θέσει δὲ καὶ τῷ μεγέθει κύκλος δεδόσθαι λέγεται, οὗ δέδοται τὸ μὲν κέντρον τῇ θέσει, ἡ δὲ ἐκ τοῦ κέντρου τῷ μεγέθει.
definitions.english_text: A circle is said to be given in position and in magnitude whose centre is given in position and whose radius is given in magnitude.

definitions.greek_text: Τμήματα κύκλων τῷ μεγέθει δεδόσθαι λέγεται, ἐν οἷς αἱ γωνίαι δεδομέναι εἰσὶ καὶ αἱ βάσεις τῶν τμημάτων τῷ μεγέθει.
definitions.english_text: Segments of circles are said to be given in magnitude in which the inscribed angles are given and the bases of the segments are given in magnitude.

definitions.greek_text: Τῇ θέσει δὲ καὶ τῷ μεγέθει τμήματα δεδόσθαι λέγεται, ἐν οἷς αἵ τε γωνίαι δεδομέναι εἰσὶ τῷ μεγέθει καὶ αἱ βάσεις τῶν τμημάτων τῇ θέσει καὶ τῷ μεγέθει.
definitions.english_text: Segments of circles are said to be given in position and in magnitude in which the inscribed angles are given in magnitude and the bases of the segments are given in position and in magnitude.

definitions.greek_text: Μέγεθος μεγέθους δοθέντι μεῖζόν ἐστιν, ὅταν, ἀφαιρεθέντος τοῦ δοθέντος, τὸ λοιπὸν τῷ αὐτῷ ἴσον ᾖ.
definitions.english_text: A magnitude is greater than a magnitude by a given magnitude when, the given magnitude being subtracted, the remainder is equal to that same magnitude.
definitions.functional_form: ExceedsByGiven(A, B) := exists GivenMagnitude(D) with A - D = B

definitions.greek_text: Μέγεθος μεγέθους δοθέντι ἔλασσόν ἐστιν, ὅταν, προστεθέντος τοῦ δοθέντος, τὸ ὅλον τῷ αὐτῷ ἴσον ᾖ.
definitions.english_text: A magnitude is less than a magnitude by a given magnitude when, the given magnitude being added, the whole is equal to that same magnitude.
definitions.functional_form: LessByGiven(A, B) := exists GivenMagnitude(D) with A + D = B

definitions.category: Affine-Ratio Excess (δοθέντι μεῖζον ἢ ἐν λόγῳ)
definitions.greek_text: Μέγεθος μεγέθους δοθέντι μεῖζόν ἐστιν ἢ ἐν λόγῳ, ὅταν, ἀφαιρεθέντος τοῦ δοθέντος, τὸ λοιπὸν πρὸς τὸ αὐτὸ λόγον ἔχῃ δεδομένον.
definitions.english_text: A magnitude is greater than a magnitude by a given magnitude than in ratio when, the given magnitude being subtracted, the remainder has a given ratio to that same magnitude.
definitions.functional_form: GreaterThanInRatio(A, B) := exists GivenMagnitude(D), GivenRatio(k) with (A - D) : B = k

definitions.category: Affine-Ratio Defect (δοθέντι ἔλασσον ἢ ἐν λόγῳ)
definitions.greek_text: Μέγεθος μεγέθους δοθέντι ἔλασσόν ἐστιν ἢ ἐν λόγῳ, ὅταν, προστεθέντος τοῦ δοθέντος, τὸ ὅλον πρὸς τὸ αὐτὸ λόγον ἔχῃ δεδομένον.
definitions.english_text: A magnitude is less than a magnitude by a given magnitude than in ratio when, the given magnitude being added, the whole has a given ratio to that same magnitude.
definitions.functional_form: LessThanInRatio(A, B) := exists GivenMagnitude(D), GivenRatio(k) with (A + D) : B = k

definitions.greek_text: Κατηγμένη ἐστὶν ἡ ἀπὸ δεδομένου σημείου ἐπὶ θέσει εὐθεῖαν ἀγομένη εὐθεῖα ἐν δεδομένῃ γωνίᾳ.
definitions.english_text: [A dropped line (katēgmenē) is the straight line drawn from a given point onto a straight line given in position in a given angle.
definitions.functional_form: Kategmene(P, L, theta) := segment from GivenPoint(P) to GivenLine(L) at GivenAngle(theta)

definitions.greek_text: Ἀνηγμένη ἐστὶν ἡ ἀπὸ δεδομένου σημείου πρὸς θέσει εὐθείᾳ ἀγομένη εὐθεῖα ἐν δεδομένῃ γωνίᾳ.
definitions.english_text: An erected line (anēgmenē) is the straight line drawn from a given point upon a straight line given in position in a given angle.
definitions.functional_form: Anegmene(P, L, theta) := ray from GivenPoint(P) on GivenLine(L) at GivenAngle(theta)

definitions.greek_text: Παρὰ θέσει ἐστὶν ἡ διὰ δεδομένου σημείου θέσει εὐθείᾳ παράλληλος ἀγομένη.
definitions.english_text: Parallel-to-position (para thesei) is the straight line drawn through a given point parallel to a straight line given in position.]
definitions.functional_form: ParaThesei(P, L) := line through GivenPoint(P) parallel to GivenLine(L)

propositions.greek_enunciation: Τῶν δεδομένων μεγεθῶν ὁ λόγος ὁ πρὸς ἄλληλα δέδοται.
propositions.english_enunciation: The ratio of given magnitudes to one another is given.
propositions.functional_signature: Given(Mag(A), Mag(B)) -> Determined(Ratio(A : B))
propositions.computational_primitive: Exact symbolic ratio evaluation sp.simplify(A / B) from known magnitudes.

propositions.greek_enunciation: Ἐὰν δεδομένον μέγεθος πρὸς ἄλλο τι μέγεθος λόγον ἔχῃ δεδομένον, δέδοται κᾀκεῖνο τῷ μεγέθει.
propositions.english_enunciation: If a given magnitude have a given ratio to some other magnitude, that other is also given in magnitude.
propositions.functional_signature: Given(Mag(A), Ratio(A : B)) -> Determined(Mag(B)) [Simson fourth-proportional diorismos]
propositions.computational_primitive: Fourth-proportional solver B = A * (D / C) when homogeneous constructibility holds.

propositions.greek_enunciation: Ἐὰν δεδομένα μεγέθη ὁποσαοῦν συντεθῇ, καὶ τὸ ἐξ αὐτῶν συγκείμενον δεδομένον ἔσται.
propositions.english_enunciation: If any multitude of given magnitudes be compounded together, the magnitude compounded out of them will also be given.
propositions.functional_signature: Given(Mag(AB), Mag(BC)) -> Determined(Mag(AB + BC))
propositions.computational_primitive: Additive closure X + Y of constructible symbolic quantities.

propositions.greek_enunciation: Ἐὰν ἀπὸ δεδομένου μεγέθους δεδομένον μέγεθος ἀφαιρεθῇ, τὸ λοιπὸν δεδομένον ἔσται.
propositions.english_enunciation: If from a given magnitude a given magnitude be subtracted, the remainder will also be given.
propositions.functional_signature: Given(Mag(AB), Mag(AC)) -> Determined(Mag(AB - AC))
propositions.computational_primitive: Subtractive closure X - Y (with X > Y) of constructible symbolic quantities.

propositions.greek_enunciation: Ἐὰν μέγεθος πρὸς ἑαυτοῦ τι μέρος λόγον ἔχῃ δεδομένον, καὶ πρὸς τὸ λοιπὸν λόγον ἕξει δεδομένον.
propositions.english_enunciation: If a magnitude have a given ratio to a part of itself, it will also have a given ratio to the remainder.
propositions.functional_signature: Given(Ratio(AB : AC)) -> Determined(Ratio(AB : (AB - AC)))
propositions.computational_primitive: Conversio rationis closure: r = A/C -> A/(A-C) = r/(r-1).

propositions.greek_enunciation: Ἐὰν δύο μεγέθη συντεθῇ πρὸς ἄλληλα λόγον ἔχοντα δεδομένον, καὶ τὸ ὅλον πρὸς ἑκάτερον αὐτῶν λόγον ἕξει δεδομένον.
propositions.english_enunciation: If two magnitudes having a given ratio to one another be compounded together, the whole magnitude will also have a given ratio to each of them.
propositions.functional_signature: Given(Ratio(AB : BC)) -> Determined(Ratio((AB+BC) : AB), Ratio((AB+BC) : BC))
propositions.computational_primitive: Compositio rationis closure: r = A/B -> (A+B)/B = r+1 and (A+B)/A = (r+1)/r.

propositions.greek_enunciation: Ἐὰν δεδομένον μέγεθος εἰς δεδομένον λόγον διαιρεθῇ, ἑκάτερον τῶν τμημάτων δεδομένον ἐστίν.
propositions.english_enunciation: If a given magnitude be divided in a given ratio, each of the segments is given.
propositions.functional_signature: Given(Mag(AB), Ratio(AC : CB)) -> Determined(Mag(AC), Mag(CB))
propositions.computational_primitive: Barycentric / internal ratio partition AC = r/(r+1)*AB, CB = 1/(r+1)*AB.

propositions.greek_enunciation: Τὰ πρὸς τὸ αὐτὸ λόγον ἔχοντα δεδομένον καὶ πρὸς ἄλληλα λόγον ἕξει δεδομένον.
propositions.english_enunciation: Magnitudes that have given ratios to the same magnitude will also have a given ratio to one another.
propositions.functional_signature: Given(Ratio(A : B), Ratio(C : B)) -> Determined(Ratio(A : C))
propositions.computational_primitive: Transitive elimination of shared reference magnitude B via ex aequali (A/C = (A/B)/(C/B)).

propositions.greek_enunciation: Ἐὰν δύο ἢ πλείονα μεγέθη πρὸς ἄλληλα λόγον ἔχῃ δεδομένον, ἔχῃ δὲ τὰ αὐτὰ μεγέθη πρὸς ἄλλα τινὰ μεγέθη λόγους δεδομένους, εἰ καὶ μὴ τοὺς αὐτούς, κᾀκεῖνα τὰ μεγέθη πρὸς ἄλληλα λόγους ἕξει δεδομένους.
propositions.english_enunciation: If two or more magnitudes have given ratios to one another, and the same magnitudes have given ratios—even if not the same—to certain other magnitudes, those other magnitudes will also have given ratios to one another.
propositions.functional_signature: Given(Ratios(A:B:C), Ratio(A:D), Ratio(B:E), Ratio(C:F)) -> Determined(Ratios(D:E:F))
propositions.computational_primitive: Diagonal scaling of a projective tuple (D, E, F) = (A/k1, B/k2, C/k3).

propositions.greek_enunciation: Ἐὰν μέγεθος μεγέθους δοθέντι μεῖζον ᾖ ἢ ἐν λόγῳ, καὶ τὸ συναμφότερον τοῦ αὐτοῦ δοθέντι μεῖζον ἔσται, ἢ ἐν λόγῳ· καὶ ἐὰν τὸ συναμφότερον τοῦ αὐτοῦ δοθέντι μεῖζον ᾖ ἢ ἐν λόγῳ, καὶ τὸ λοιπὸν τοῦ αὐτοῦ ἤτοι δοθέντι μεῖζόν ἐστιν ἢ ἐν λόγῳ, ἢ τὸ λοιπὸν μετὰ τοῦ ἑξῆς, πρὸς ὃ τὸ ἕτερον λόγον ἔχει δεδομένον, δοθέν ἐστιν.
propositions.english_enunciation: If a magnitude be greater than a magnitude by a given magnitude than in ratio, the compounded magnitude will also be greater than the same by a given magnitude than in ratio; and if the compounded magnitude be greater than the same by a given magnitude than in ratio, either the remainder is also greater than the same by a given magnitude than in ratio, or the remainder together with the following magnitude to which the other has a given ratio is given.
given: GreaterThanInRatio(AB, BC): (AB - D) : BC = k [and converse on AC, BC]
determined: GreaterThanInRatio(AC, BC) [and converse Trichotomy on AB, BC]
propositions.functional_signature: Given((AB - D) : BC = k) <-> Determined(((AB+BC) - D) : BC = k+1 | (AB + BE = D where BC:BE given))
propositions.computational_primitive: Affine-ratio composition and converse bifurcation depending on whether given offset D < AB or D > AB.

propositions.greek_enunciation: Ἐὰν μέγεθος μεγέθους δοθέντι μεῖζον ᾖ ἢ ἐν λόγῳ, τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ συναμφοτέρου δοθέντι μεῖζον ἔσται ἢ ἐν λόγῳ, καὶ ἐὰν τὸ αὐτὸ συναμφοτέρου δοθέντι μεῖζον ᾖ ἢ ἐν λόγῳ, τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ τοῦ λοιποῦ δοθέντι μεῖζον ἔσται ἢ ἐν λόγῳ.
propositions.english_enunciation: If a magnitude be greater than a magnitude by a given magnitude than in ratio, the same will also be greater than the compounded magnitude by a given magnitude than in ratio; and if the same be greater than the compounded magnitude by a given magnitude than in ratio, the same will also be greater than the remainder by a given magnitude than in ratio.
given: GreaterThanInRatio(AB, BC): (AB - D) : BC = k [and converse on AB, AC]
determined: GreaterThanInRatio(AB, AB + BC) [and converse GreaterThanInRatio(AB, BC)]
propositions.functional_signature: Given((AB - D) : BC = k) <-> Determined((AB - k/(k+1)*D) : (AB + BC) = k/(k+1))
propositions.computational_primitive: Bidirectional affine-linear substitution solving BC = (AB - D)/k into AB + BC and back.

propositions.greek_enunciation: Ἐὰν ᾖ τρία μεγέθη καὶ τὸ μὲν πρῶτον μετὰ τοῦ δευτέρου ᾖ δοθέν, ᾖ δὲ καὶ τὸ δεύτερον μετὰ τοῦ τρίτου δοθέν, τὸ πρῶτον τῷ τρίτῳ ἤτοι ἴσον ἐστίν, ἢ τὸ ἕτερον τοῦ ἑτέρου δοθέντι μεῖζόν ἐστιν.
propositions.english_enunciation: If there be three magnitudes, and the first together with the second be given, and the second together with the third be also given, then either the first is equal to the third, or one exceeds the other by a given magnitude.
propositions.functional_signature: Given(Mag(A + B), Mag(B + C)) -> Determined(A = C | ExceedsByGiven(A, C))
propositions.computational_primitive: Elimination of common summand B: A - C = (A + B) - (B + C).

propositions.greek_enunciation: Ἐὰν ᾖ τρία μεγέθη, καὶ τὸ μὲν πρῶτον πρὸς τὸ δεύτερον λόγον ἔχῃ δεδομένον, τὸ δὲ δεύτερον τοῦ τρίτου δοθέντι μεῖζον ᾖ ἢ ἐν λόγῳ, καὶ τὸ πρῶτον τοῦ τρίτου δοθέντι μεῖζον ἔσται ἢ ἐν λόγῳ.
propositions.english_enunciation: If there be three magnitudes, and the first have to the second a given ratio, while the second is greater than the third by a given magnitude than in ratio, the first will also be greater than the third by a given magnitude than in ratio.
propositions.functional_signature: Given(Ratio(A : B) = r, (B - F) : C = k) -> Determined((A - r*F) : C = r*k)
propositions.computational_primitive: Scalar multiplication of an affine-ratio relation A = r*B = r*F + (r*k)*C.

propositions.greek_enunciation: Ἐὰν δύο μεγέθη πρὸς ἄλληλα λόγον ἔχῃ δεδομένον, καὶ προστεθῇ ἑκατέρῳ αὐτῶν δεδομένον μέγεθος, τὰ ὅλα πρὸς ἄλληλα ἤτοι λόγον ἕξει δεδομένον, ἢ τὸ ἕτερον τοῦ ἑτέρου δοθέντι μεῖζόν ἐστιν ἢ ἐν λόγῳ.
propositions.english_enunciation: If two magnitudes have a given ratio to one another, and a given magnitude be added to each of them, either the wholes will still have a given ratio to one another, or one will be greater than the other by a given magnitude than in ratio.
propositions.functional_signature: Given(Ratio(A : C) = r, Mag(d1), Mag(d2)) -> Determined(Ratio(A+d1 : C+d2) | GreaterThanInRatio)
propositions.computational_primitive: Affine shift of proportional variables: (A+d1) - r*(C+d2) = d1 - r*d2.

propositions.greek_enunciation: Ἐὰν δύο μεγέθη πρὸς ἄλληλα λόγον ἔχῃ δεδομένον καὶ ἀφαιρεθῇ ἀπὸ ἑκατέρου αὐτῶν δεδομένον μέγεθος, τὰ λοιπὰ πρὸς ἄλληλα ἤτοι λόγον ἕξει δεδομένον, ἢ τὸ ἕτερον τοῦ ἑτέρου δοθέντι μεῖζόν ἐστιν ἢ ἐν λόγῳ.
propositions.english_enunciation: If two magnitudes have a given ratio to one another, and a given magnitude be subtracted from each of them, either the remainders will have a given ratio to one another, or one will be greater than the other by a given magnitude than in ratio.
propositions.functional_signature: Given(Ratio(A : C) = r, Mag(d1), Mag(d2)) -> Determined(Ratio(A-d1 : C-d2) | GreaterThanInRatio)
propositions.computational_primitive: Subtractive affine shift: (A-d1) - r*(C-d2) = r*d2 - d1.

propositions.greek_enunciation: Ἐὰν δύο μεγέθη πρὸς ἄλληλα λόγον ἔχῃ δεδομένον, καὶ ἀπὸ μὲν τοῦ ἑνὸς αὐτῶν δεδομένον μέγεθος ἀφαιρεθῇ, τῷ δὲ ἑτέρῳ αὐτῶν δεδομένον μέγεθος προστεθῇ, τὸ ὅλον τοῦ λοιποῦ δοθέντι μεῖζον ἔσται ἢ ἐν λόγῳ.
propositions.english_enunciation: If two magnitudes have a given ratio to one another, and from one of them a given magnitude be subtracted while to the other a given magnitude be added, the whole will be greater than the remainder by a given magnitude than in ratio.
propositions.functional_signature: Given(Ratio(A : C) = r, Mag(d1), Mag(d2)) -> Determined(((A+d2) - (r*d1+d2)) : (C-d1) = r)
propositions.computational_primitive: Mixed affine shift: A + d2 = r*(C - d1) + (r*d1 + d2), offset strictly positive.

propositions.greek_enunciation: Ἐὰν ᾖ τρία μεγέθη, καὶ τὸ πρῶτον τοῦ δευτέρου δοθέντι μεῖζον ᾖ ἢ ἐν λόγῳ, ᾖ δὲ καὶ τὸ τρίτον τοῦ αὐτοῦ δοθέντι μεῖζον ἢ ἐν λόγῳ, τὸ πρῶτον πρὸς τὸ τρίτον ἤτοι λόγον ἕξει δεδομένον, ἢ τὸ ἕτερον τοῦ ἑτέρου δοθέντι μεῖζον ἔσται ἢ ἐν λόγῳ.
propositions.english_enunciation: If there be three magnitudes, and the first be greater than the second by a given magnitude than in ratio, and the third be also greater than the same second by a given magnitude than in ratio, then either the first has a given ratio to the third, or one is greater than the other by a given magnitude than in ratio.
propositions.functional_signature: Given((A - d1):B = k1, (C - d2):B = k2) -> Determined(Ratio(A:C) | GreaterThanInRatio(A, C))
propositions.computational_primitive: Elimination of parameter B between two affine-linear equations A = d1 + k1*B, C = d2 + k2*B.

propositions.greek_enunciation: Ἐὰν ᾖ τρία μεγέθη, ἓν δὲ αὐτῶν ἑκατέρου τῶν λοιπῶν δοθέντι μεῖζον ᾖ ἢ ἐν λόγῳ, τὰ λοιπὰ δύο πρὸς ἄλληλα ἤτοι λόγον ἕξει δεδομένον, ἢ τὸ ἕτερον τοῦ ἑτέρου δοθέντι μεῖζόν ἐστιν ἢ ἐν λόγῳ.
propositions.english_enunciation: If there be three magnitudes, and one of them be greater than each of the remaining two by a given magnitude than in ratio, the remaining two will either have a given ratio to one another, or one is greater than the other by a given magnitude than in ratio.
